chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abi Khadija, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The man should not oil (massage) every day. The man should look shaggier and he should not look smooth like a woman.

key_terms.شَعِثاً: shaggy; having rough or unkempt hair/beard
key_terms.مُتَزَلِّقاً: smooth; sleek; slippery (referring to skin or hair)
key_terms.يَدَّهِنُ: to apply oil or unguent; to groom excessively

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on men oiling their hair or body daily?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to caution against *al-dahin* (excessive grooming with oil), linking it to *al-tashabbuh* (imitation of the opposite gender). The imagery of 'shaggy' (*sha'ith*) versus 'slippery/smooth' (*mutazallaq*) reflects the cultural context of pre-Islamic and early Islamic Arabia, where excessive oiling was associated with effeminacy or vanity, thereby preserving distinct masculine identity and modesty.
